Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Elevated tail latency for MedVent inference – mitigation plan and timeline

Hi Jake / MedVent team,

We wanted to let you know we observed an increase in p95/p99 tail latency on the hosted inference endpoint backing your document-extraction workflow (model: open-a2-16k). Impact started at ~08:30 PDT this morning and has affected a subset of requests with longer sequence lengths and mixed batch sizes.

What we're doing now:
- We opened an SRE bridge and rolled a targeted kernel rollback for affected runtime shards.
- Enabled a temporary per-customer batching cap for your account to reduce variance.
- Publishing a short status update on our status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2026-11-03-medvent-latency (live).

Next update: We will send an internal mitigation summary in ~60 minutes and a customer update within 2 hours with estimated time to full resolution.

Attachments: initial latency graphs attached (2026-11-03_medvent_latency_graphs.png).

Sorry for the disruption — we understand this affects throughput for your nightly processing window. If you can share any particularly high-priority routes (route names or request ids) we will prioritize them.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Notice: Elevated tail latency for MedVent inference – mitigation plan and timeline

Marissa — quick internal notes / action items (SRE + Runtime):

Summary: regression in the continuous-batching kernel selection logic that misclassifies mixed-length requests, causing larger-than-expected batches and KV cache thrash under certain distributions. Repro on staging with a replayed MedVent trace.

Immediate mitigation (done / in progress):
- Rolled kernel version 6.3.1 -> 6.2.8 for the affected shard pool (done, ~09:30 PST).
- Applied a per-account max_batch_tokens override for MedVent (temporary) to keep latency stable.
- Disabled a mem-opt heuristic that was causing aggressive KV pruning under mixed sequences.

Planned next steps (30–90 min):
- Run a rolling restart across remaining shards to ensure consistent kernel across the pool (Ben).
- Upload and attach heap profiles + kernel logs for postmortem (Monica) — see heap_profiles_nov03.zip.
- Prepare a short customer-facing RCA draft for Marissa to share after containment.

Please confirm the nightly window requirement from the customer (200 req/min) and whether the temporary cap meets it — if not, we can provision additional capacity for the window.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@medvent.com>, MedVent Support <support@medvent.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: RESOLVED: Tail latency incident – summary & next steps

Hi Jake / MedVent team,

Update: The immediate issue is resolved as of 12:45 PDT on 2026-11-04. We validated request latency over the last 60 minutes across your routes and are no longer seeing the elevated p95/p99 spike.

Brief root cause (summary):
- A kernel selection regression introduced a batching decision that grouped long-sequence and short-sequence requests into the same batch. That caused intermittent cache evictions and a tail-latency amplification for requests with large sequences.
- The regression was triggered by a heuristic change in 6.3.1 that is now rolled back to 6.2.8 for the affected pool.

What we did:
- Rolled back to 6.2.8 and ran rolling restarts (completed).
- Applied a temporary per-account max_batch_tokens limit for MedVent during your nightly window (02:00 UTC) and confirmed 220 req/min headroom for that window.
- Collected profiles and logs; attached incident_summary_medvent_20261104.csv and heap_profiles_nov03.zip for your postmortem review.

Offers and next steps:
- We will publish a mitigation postmortem (draft link: https://docs.redwood.inference/internal/postmortems/MV-2026-11-03-latency) and propose a 30-min joint RCA call next week. Would Thursday 2026-11-10 10:00 PDT work?
- Regarding SLA: we are initiating a credit review given the observed timeouts; we will follow up with account credits within 5 business days.

If you need an immediate escalation or an earlier call, reply and we will prioritize. Thanks again for your patience while we resolved this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
